newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian coffee official downplays strike threat.
newsitem.headline: Colombian coffee official downplays strike threat.

text.p: A leader of Colombia's independent coffee growers' association, Unidad Cafetera Nacional, played down local media reports that growers may move to declare a strike later this week.

Jorge Enrique Robledo, the association's national coordinator, said about 500 delegates from 100 coffee-growing areas across Colombia would meet Wednesday in the eastern city of Pereira to discuss a variety of demands, including longstanding calls for debt relief from the government.
But contrary to Colombian news radio reports, he said the idea of a work stoppage was not on the agenda for the meeting.
National Coffee Growers Federation raised Colombia's internal coffee price to 248,125 pesos per 125-kg load last week to bring it closer into line with recent increases in world market prices.
Robledo said this failed to quell widespread discontent among growers, however, since it fell far short of the Unidad Cafetera's call for a minimum price of 270,000 pesos.

The main discussion item at Wednesday's meeting would be relief for the estimated 40,000 to 50,000 owners of small plantations across Colombia who face legal problems, or the possible loss of their farms, because of past-due debts, Robledo said.
He stressed "the situation has gone from bad to worse" for many impoverished coffee farmers and work stoppages or public protest could not be ruled out in the future.
"It's up to the delegates," he said. "They're the ones who will make the decisions about what policy to follow." ((--Juan Guillermo Londoo, Bogota newsroom, 571 610 7944))
